background: ABN AMRO is a Dutch retail, private and commercial bank, part-owned by the Dutch state since its rescue, funded largely by domestic deposits and lending mainly on Dutch residential mortgages and to Northwest European businesses.
synthesis: Rated A+ on average across all three, the weakest of them at A, with one on a positive outlook after a two-notch upgrade by one of the three on 12 May 2026; that positive outlook was maintained on 16 Sep 2026. Liquidity is the strength, with LCR of 159% above the peer median and NSFR of 138% in the top quarter of EU and Nordic banks. Capital is the weaker side: CET1 of 15.3% and leverage of 4.9% both sit below the peer median. Since 30 Jun 2025 CET1 has risen 0.8 points and LCR 14 points, while leverage has fallen 0.6 points.
